result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B lists all ten signals in their original order with exactly the supplied meanings, in a clean table where the meaning column can be covered. Its one usage note is short. A has a useful separate self-test section, but it regroups the signals out of order and adds a sub-description to every meaning, some of which go beyond the supplied wording (for example, 'available after arrival' for M-10). That adds explanation to a list that has to be memorized exactly. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): A shows all ten signals in their original order with the exact supplied meanings, in a clean table. You can cover either column to quiz yourself in both directions, and its only usage note is one short line. B also keeps the meanings correct and adds a fill-in self-test, but it regroups the signals out of order and adds a made-up explanation under each one (for example, 'available after arrival' for M-10). Those extras dilute direct recall, and B's self-test sits on the same page as the answers.
